Nav.agentsAwaiting: The Numo agent is waiting for your answer
Nav.syncPromptText:
Synchronize the local git repo with `origin` so they are strictly identical (0 commits ahead, 0 behind on the current branch).

1. Run `git fetch --all --prune`, then compare the local branch to its upstream.
2. If they have diverged, rebase my local commits on top of the upstream (linear history, no merge commit).
3. Review the resulting history before pushing, then push as a fast-forward. Only use `--force-with-lease` if strictly necessary, and warn me first.
4. Finish by confirming the state: 0 ahead / 0 behind.

Don't touch my uncommitted files; if a rebase conflict occurs, stop and show me the conflict.

Privacy.collectedIntro: When you use minddy, we process the following data:
Privacy.dataAccountDesc: email address, user id, display name and profile picture (via Supabase Auth). If you sign in with Google or GitHub, those services pass us your email, name and profile picture; no password is ever shared with us
Privacy.dataContentDesc: the projects, issues, plans, comments and attachments you create, stored in our database and in Supabase Storage
Privacy.dataUsageDesc: pages visited and actions performed in the application (via PostHog — see the “Usage measurement” section below for what applies depending on your cookie choice), plus aggregated traffic measurement with no cookie and no persistent identifier (Vercel Analytics)
Privacy.dataAIDesc: content sent to the Numo assistant, to dictation and to the coding agent — including the code of the linked repository during an agent run — is transmitted to OpenRouter for processing
Privacy.dataGitDesc: access tokens for your GitHub or GitLab repositories are encrypted (AES-256-GCM) before storage. We only reach the repository when you trigger an action that requires it

Privacy.dataFeedbackDesc: email address verified by one-time code, votes and posted feedback. Verification emails are delivered by Resend

Privacy.legalBasisConsentDesc: analytics cookies (PostHog), which link your successive visits — collected via the consent banner and revocable at any time
Privacy.legalBasisObligationDesc: retention of accounting and invoicing records
Privacy.retentionAccountDesc: kept until your account is deleted
Privacy.retentionContentDesc: kept until you delete it or until your account is closed
Privacy.retentionAgentDesc: the execution state (messages exchanged with the model, code excerpts) is kept for the duration of the run and its resumptions; afterwards only the metadata (branch, pull request, status) stays attached to the issue
Privacy.retentionFeedbackDesc: kept while the board is active, then deleted when the board is closed or at its publisher's request
Privacy.retentionBillingDesc: as required by law (10 years for accounting records)
Privacy.transfersText: Your data is hosted within the European Union (Supabase EU region, Ireland). The application is hosted by Vercel (a company based in the United States); any transfers to third countries are covered by appropriate safeguards (Standard Contractual Clauses). Data processing agreements (DPAs) are in place with our sub-processors.
Privacy.transfersProcessors: Sub-processors involved: <supabase>Supabase</supabase> (database, storage, authentication), <vercel>Vercel</vercel> (application hosting, agent execution environments, custom domains), <stripe>Stripe</stripe> (payment), <openrouter>OpenRouter</openrouter> (AI processing), <posthog>PostHog</posthog> (analytics, with consent), <resend>Resend</resend> (transactional email).
Privacy.transfersAuth: If you choose to sign in with Google or GitHub, those services handle your authentication as independent controllers, under their own policies. If you link a GitHub or GitLab repository, access to that repository happens at your initiative and under your responsibility.
Privacy.processorTitle: Feedback boards: minddy as a processor
Privacy.processorP1: When you open a public feedback board, you become the controller for the data of the people who take part in it, and minddy acts as a processor: we process that data only to provide you with the board, on your instructions.
Privacy.processorP2: Categories involved: verified email address, votes, published feedback and related exchanges. We never use them for marketing, nor to train models. You can request their deletion at any time; they are deleted along with the board.
Privacy.agentText: When you trigger the coding agent, the linked repository is cloned into an isolated, ephemeral virtual machine provided by Vercel (Sandbox), destroyed at the end of the run. The code needed for the task is sent to the model through OpenRouter. minddy keeps no copy of the repository beyond the run.
Privacy.thirdPartyText: When you authorize a third-party application (an AI assistant over MCP, for example), it receives an access token and can read and modify your account's data within the permissions granted. Privacy.rightComplaint: Right to lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority
Privacy.rightsContact: To exercise these rights, write to us at <email>hello@minddy.app</email>. If a dispute remains unresolved, you may refer the matter to the <cnil>CNIL</cnil>.
Privacy.breachText: In the event of a personal data breach likely to result in a high risk to your rights and freedoms, we will notify you without undue delay, along with the competent supervisory authority (CNIL), in accordance with articles 33 and 34 of the GDPR.
Privacy.analyticsIntro: minddy measures how the service is used with PostHog, hosted in the European Union. What we collect depends on your choice on the cookie banner, across three states:
Privacy.analyticsAnonymous: Until you answer the banner: measurement is anonymous and cookieless. Nothing is written to your device — no cookie, no local storage — and the measurement identifier disappears when you close the tab. Two visits therefore cannot be linked to one another. This measurement relies on our legitimate interest in understanding how the service is used; it requires no prior consent because it does not access your device.
Privacy.analyticsAccepted: If you accept: a cookie is set, which lets us link your successive visits and, when you are signed in, attach them to your account so we can understand usage journeys over time.
Privacy.analyticsDeclined: If you decline: no usage data is collected at all, neither anonymous nor identified.
Privacy.analyticsMinimization: In every case, we send PostHog only a closed list of technical events that we defined ourselves (for example “an issue was created”, with its status and priority). The content you type never leaves minddy: no issue titles or descriptions, no comments, no messages to the assistant, no file names. Automatic click capture and on-screen session recording are disabled.

Cookies.title: Cookie policy
Cookies.whatText: A cookie is a small text file stored by your browser when you visit a website. It lets the site remember information about your visit, such as your preferences or your login session.
Cookies.essentialDesc: These cookies are essential for the service to work. They cannot be disabled.
Cookies.analyticDesc: These cookies let us measure usage and improve the service. They are only set with your consent. Before you choose, measurement already happens but without any cookie — see “Cookieless traffic measurement” below.
Cookies.noCookieText: Two measurements run without writing anything to your device. Vercel Analytics measures page traffic with no cookie and no persistent identifier. PostHog runs in that same cookieless mode until you answer the banner: the measurement identifier lives in memory only and disappears when you close the tab, so two visits cannot be linked. No prior consent is required for these, because they do not access your device. If you accept the banner, PostHog then sets the cookie described in the table above; if you decline, it stops collecting entirely.
Cookies.localStorageDesc: Values saved by your browser to remember your preferences and interface state. They never leave your device.
Cookies.localStorageKey1Purpose: Your consent choice for analytics cookies
Cookies.localStorageKey2Purpose: Your display theme (light, dark or system)
Cookies.localStorageKey3Purpose: Drafts of issues and comments not yet submitted
Cookies.localStorageKey4Purpose: The view selected on each board
Cookies.localStorageKey5Purpose: A feedback post being written on a public board
Cookies.thirdPartyText: minddy uses no advertising cookies and no cross-site trackers. No data is shared with advertising networks.
Cookies.preferencesText: On your first visit, a banner lets you accept or decline analytics cookies. You can change that choice at any time:
Cookies.preferencesOption1: Through your browser settings (deleting or blocking cookies)
Cookies.preferencesOption2: By clearing this site's local storage, which brings the banner back
Cookies.preferencesOption3: By writing to <email>hello@minddy.app</email> for any request about your data
Cookies.preferencesNote: Note: disabling strictly necessary cookies prevents access to the service.

Landing.metaTitle: minddy — the issue tracker your agents drive
Landing.metaDescription: A minimal issue tracker wired to your coding agents over MCP: they read the issue, write their plan, tick the tasks off and open the pull request.
Landing.heroTitleBefore: minddy is the issue tracker your agents
Landing.heroSubtitle: You write the issue. Your coding agent reads it, writes its plan, ticks the tasks off as it goes, then opens the pull request. You keep the overview.
Landing.heroNote: Free for up to 2 projects. No credit card.
Landing.workflowSubtitle: One thread, from the moment you describe the work to the moment you read the diff.
Landing.workflow_write_body: A title, two sentences, a priority. The agent turns the description into an implementation plan: ordered tasks naming the actual files to touch, stored on the issue itself.
Landing.workflow_run_body: The run happens in an isolated environment. Each task flips to “in progress”, then “done”, while it works — you follow along without rereading the whole thread.
Landing.workflow_review_body: The pull request lands on the issue with its description and its diff, file by file. You review, you comment, you merge.
Landing.agentsTitle: Your agents write to minddy, not the other way around
Landing.agentsSubtitle: minddy exposes an MCP server. Your agents read and update the tracker themselves — no more issues brought up to date by hand three days later.
Landing.agentsCapability_read: Read an issue with its full context: description, plan, comments, attachments, history.
Landing.agentsCapability_plan: Write the implementation plan onto the issue, then tick each task off along the way.
Landing.agentsCapability_track: Change status, priority, assignee, objective or cycle.
Landing.agentsCapability_create: Create issues and objectives, and link them to each other.
Landing.agentsCapability_comment: Report back in a comment, with the pull request and its diff attached.
Landing.agentsInstallNote: No key to copy: authorization goes through OAuth, your agent opens the browser on first use.
Landing.numoSubtitle: The assistant lives in the app, not in a tab next door. It reads your projects, acts on them and hands you back the wheel: you talk to it like someone who has already read the board.
Landing.numoCapability_find_body: “What's waiting in triage?”, “where are we on payments?” — it goes through the issues, objectives, comments and user feedback before answering.
Landing.numoCapability_act_body: Create an issue, change ten statuses at once, assign, schedule, file under an objective, save a filtered view: what you'd do by hand, in one sentence.
Landing.numoCapability_plan_body: It writes an issue's implementation plan, launches the coding agent on it, and brings you the pull request once it's ready.
Landing.numoCapability_context_body: The issue, board or cycle in front of you is its context — nothing to paste back in. In a comment thread, mention it and it answers right there.
Landing.numoExample_assign: Assign the urgent issues to me
Landing.numoExample_view: Create a view of urgent bugs
Landing.numoExample_plan: Write the plan for MIN-42 and launch an agent on it
Landing.voiceTitle: Wherever you'd type, you can just talk
Landing.voiceSubtitle: A mic button next to every field. You speak, the sentence gets written. And when it's an issue, what you said doesn't only land in the description: Numo files it into the right fields.
Landing.voice_create_body: Right when you create the issue, before you even have a title. You dictate one sentence, the form comes back filled, and all that is left is to read it over.
Landing.voice_edit_body: The issue is open, you keep going: “move it to in progress and add that the webhook returns a 500”. The fields move in front of you, without opening a single menu.
Landing.voice_everywhere_body: Comments, pull request reviews, notebook entries, instructions to Numo: the same mic button, up to 90 seconds per take.
Landing.voiceNote: Transcription follows your interface language. Nothing to install, nothing to tune — you just allow the mic once.
Landing.voiceFigureQuote: “<f1>Bug on Stripe payments</f1>, <f2>high priority</f2>, <f3>due Friday</f3>, <f4>assign it to Léa</f4>.”
Landing.voiceFigureCaption: One seven-second take. No menu opened, no field filled by hand.
Landing.scratchpadTitle: Everything that isn't an issue yet
Landing.scratchpadSubtitle: One personal note, shared across all your projects. It opens from anywhere with G then N and closes just as fast: the notes file you kept open in your editor, except your agents can read this one.
Landing.scratchpadPoint_write: Headings, checkboxes, and “/” for the rest: add a task, or dictate it.
Landing.scratchpadPoint_prompt: Copy a line, a section or the whole notebook as a prompt, ready to paste into your agent.
Landing.scratchpadPoint_agent: Or launch the coding agent straight from a section, without going through an issue.
Landing.scratchpadPoint_promote: A note that outgrows the notebook becomes an issue: Numo converts it, then takes it off the list.
Landing.scratchpadPoint_mcp: Your agents reach it over MCP too: they read the notebook, add tasks and tick off what they've finished.
Landing.feedbackTitle: A public board where your users ask, and vote
Landing.feedbackSubtitle: A public page — on your own domain if you want — where feedback arrives, groups itself and sorts by votes. Your users never set foot in your tracker, and you stop triaging the same request three times.
Landing.feedbackCaptionBoard: Public side: people suggest, vote, and see what the team did about it.
Landing.feedbackCaptionInbox: Team side: the same request, its votes, and what you can do with it.
Landing.feedback_post_body: An email, a six-digit code, and it's published — under a pseudonym on the board. Wire up SSO from your app and your signed-in users skip even that.
Landing.feedback_dedupe_body: On submission, near-identical requests are offered to vote on rather than posted again. The ones that slip through, you merge: votes add up, one identity is one voice.
Landing.feedback_decide_body: You answer publicly on behalf of the team, promote the request to an issue, or link it to an issue that already exists.
Landing.feedback_status_body: Open, Planned, In progress, Shipped: the moment the linked issue moves, the public board moves with it. Nothing left to announce by hand.
Landing.feedbackNote: Spam is turned away before publication, and sensitive reports — a vulnerability, personal data — come to you first. Feedback can also arrive through the API, or be entered on behalf of a user who wrote to you elsewhere.
Landing.featuresSubtitle: A tracker you open without dread: a handful of screens, keyboard shortcuts everywhere, and nothing to configure before you start.
Landing.featuresCaptionCycle: Your fortnight, across every project: what you are working on right now.
Landing.featuresCaptionPalette: ⌘K for everything: search, create, change a status, launch an agent.
Landing.feature_board_body: List or columns, grouped by status, priority or objective. Saved filters, multi-select and bulk actions from the keyboard.
Landing.feature_cycles_body: A personal fortnight that cuts across all your projects. Fill it yourself, or let it compose itself.
Landing.feature_triage_body: Anything coming from outside lands in triage. You accept, reclassify or close it — nothing slips into the backlog behind your back.
Landing.feature_palette_body: Every action from the keyboard, including on a multi-selection. The mouse becomes optional.
Landing.pricingSubtitle: What you pay for is the AI usage included in your plan — agents, Numo, dictation, feedback triage.
Landing.pricingNote: Payment through Stripe. Switch plans or cancel at any time.
Landing.faq_agents_q: Which coding agents can I connect?
Landing.faq_agents_a: Any agent that speaks MCP: Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, VS Code and Windsurf. Connecting takes one command, and authorization happens over OAuth — no key to copy.
Landing.faq_byok_q: Can I use my own API key?
Landing.faq_byok_a: Yes. By default runs draw on the usage included in your plan; you can also plug in your own key (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, OpenRouter or a compatible endpoint) and stop drawing on it entirely.
Landing.faq_usage_q: How does the included AI usage work?
Landing.faq_usage_a: Every plan includes a monthly budget covering coding agents, Numo, dictation and feedback processing. You can see what has been spent at any time, action by action and by feature.
Landing.faq_data_a: It is never sold or used for advertising. You can export your issues and request deletion of your account at any time; the privacy page details every processing operation.
Landing.faq_team_q: Does it work with a team?
Landing.faq_team_a: Yes, from the Pro plan on: you invite members into your projects, each with their own account. Free and Go are built for working solo.
Landing.faq_migrate_q: I'm coming from Linear or Jira — how do I migrate?
Landing.faq_migrate_a: You import the Linear or Jira CSV export from the project settings: titles, descriptions, statuses, priorities and assignees all come across.
Landing.ctaTitle: Ready to hand over your first issue?
Landing.ctaSubtitle: Create a project, write an issue, connect your agent. There is nothing else to set up.
Landing.footerTagline: The minimal issue tracker, wired to your coding agents.

Pricing.metaDescription: Free to start, then a monthly subscription sized to the AI usage you need. Unlimited projects and issues from the first paid plan.
Pricing.heroTitle: Pricing that fits in three lines
Pricing.heroSubtitle: Free to start. A subscription as soon as you want coding agents, and one step up to work with other people.
Pricing.comparisonSubtitle: The limits the product actually enforces, line by line.
Pricing.faq_usage_a: Coding agent runs, conversations with Numo, voice dictation and automatic feedback processing. The rest of the tracker — issues, board, cycles, triage — consumes nothing.
Pricing.faq_overage_q: What happens if I run out of budget?
Pricing.faq_overage_a: AI features pause until renewal, and the tracker keeps working as usual. Overages are never billed to you: no surprise invoice.
Pricing.faq_change_q: Can I switch plans along the way?
Pricing.faq_change_a: Yes, at any time, from your account's billing page. Moving to annual or back to monthly goes through the Stripe portal, prorated.
Pricing.faq_refund_a: Yes, in one click from the Stripe portal. Your subscription stays active until the end of the period you already paid for, then your account returns to the free plan.
